label: organizations confirmed breached by name
detail: Still none by name, and the one vendor account of a victim is gone: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 retracted its Oct 23 report of an AI-agent-like intrusion at a European government agency on Oct 25 (2:15 p.m. PT), saying it 'is unable to confirm that initial access is associated with the specific PHP2Shell CVEs'. What stands instead, as of Oct 26, is narrower and firmer: a honeypot run by Perplexity's detection lead Adel Karimi recorded confirmed code execution against an unpatched Apache mod_php server, which Expel's Marcus Hutchins calls the highest-quality in-the-wild confirmation so far; Dataminr says activity before it showed 'no known compromises'. The earlier 0x4D31 honeypot report (35 shells, three decoys, Oct 24) is Karimi's. Sophos retracted its one earlier claim on Oct 22. Proof the technique works against real unpatched servers; still no victim.

label: exploit attempts seen by Cloudflare
detail: Tens of thousands within 45 minutes of disclosure, millions by Oct 22. TU Delft's live dashboard counts 41,907 exploitation requests from 586 source IPs in 68 countries against its own honeypots and telescope between Oct 21 and 11:04 UTC Oct 26, 171 of them sending code or a dropper. Some attempts try to enlist servers into a Mirai botnet variant (Potassium); no infection count has been published.
source_label: The Hacker News, Oct 23; TU Delft, Oct 26

label: UK government digital services confirmed unavailable
detail: Plus four partially unavailable, mostly precautionary. The NCSC has issued about 50,000 warnings.

label: PHP services Censys counts on affected versions
detail: As of Oct 22, against about 1 million on a fixed release; Censys separately assesses 34.4 million services on 3.1 million hosts as vulnerable; Bitsight (Oct 25, via The Hacker News) counts nearly 37 million internet-facing systems running PHP or PHP-related software. Versions before 8.2 will never get an official fix.

label: of 2.6M exposed PHP hosts VulnCheck rates vulnerable or likely vulnerable
detail: 2,608,039 internet-facing hosts as of Oct 23: 1,474,985 advertise a version below the fixed build, 1,133,000 hide their version, 700,000+ run PHP 3.x to 7.3. Qualys separately saw 199,000 instances patched in the first 12 hours and counts about 110 million on end-of-life versions.

label: on CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
detail: Not listed as of Monday morning, per SecurityWeek (09:30 ET Oct 26); this run could not open the feed itself. Last opened directly at 07:08 ET Oct 26: catalog version 2026.10.23, released Oct 23 at 19:30 UTC, 1,756 entries, none of the three PHP CVEs; the newest additions are still the Oct 23 Arista and Collabora entries. No federal emergency directive reported. A listing is CISA's formal verdict that exploitation is real; the Oct 26 honeypot confirmation is the kind of evidence one rests on.
source_label: CISA KEV catalog, version 2026.10.23, checked Oct 26
